title: Reentrant superconductivity enabled by spin-orbit coupling: Application to UTe$_2$
authors: Changhee Lee, Nico A. Hackner, Daniel F. Agterberg, P. M. R. Brydon
abstract: Reentrant superconductivity has been understood primarily in terms of the Jaccarino-Peter field-compensation effect or from a change of the strength in the pairing interaction. However, neither mechanism appears able to entirely explain the remarkable phase diagram of UTe$_2$. Here we propose a generic theory of the field-enhancement of opposite-spin Cooper pairings which does not necessitate the coexistence of magnetism or the vicinity of a magnetic quantum critical point. Our analytical treatment shows that the reentrance has its origin in the interplay of the sublattice degrees of freedom and spin-orbit coupling, which can can strikingly enhance opposite-spin Cooper pairings at strong Zeeman fields. Based on these results, we show that a pairing state with B$_{3u}$ symmetry can reproduce the highly anisotropic phase diagram of the reentrant superconducting state of UTe$_2$.
summary: This theoretical work explains the unusual reentrant superconducting phase in UTe2 by proposing that spin-orbit coupling interacting with sublattice structure is the key driver. The theory predicts that strong magnetic fields enhance opposite-spin Cooper pairing when band hybridization causes an anticrossing, successfully reproducing the material's anisotropic phase diagram.
main_problem: The paper aims to explain the reentrant superconductivity observed in UTe2 under a magnetic field, as standard mechanisms fail to account for its complex phase diagram.
main_result: Reentrance is attributed to the interplay between sublattice degrees of freedom and spin-orbit coupling (SOC), which enhances opposite-spin Cooper pairing at high fields via an anticrossing mechanism.
method: The authors developed a generic theory involving analytical treatment of the superconducting pairing susceptibility ($\chi$) derived from a tight-binding Hamiltonian incorporating SOC and Zeeman coupling.
model_or_system: The system is UTe2, modeled using an effective Hamiltonian that includes hopping terms, staggered spin-orbit coupling, and Zeeman coupling acting on sublattice degrees of freedom. The theory focuses on opposite-spin Cooper pairing channels.
key_observables: Pairing susceptibility ($\chi$) as a function of magnetic field strength and angle; the superconducting phase diagram vs. B.
important_parameters: Spin-orbit coupling (SOC) strength, Zeeman field magnitude ($B$), sublattice hopping parameters, and the symmetry of the pairing state ($B_{3u}$).
main_assumptions: The theory assumes that the reentrance is driven by SOC interplay rather than magnetism or quantum critical points; it also uses a simplified description of f-electron physics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the magnetic field-angle superconducting phase diagram showing $\chi$, and band structure evolution demonstrating an anticrossing surface responsible for pairing enhancement at high fields.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the failure of existing models to proposing a generic theory based on SOC interplay. It details the Hamiltonian, analyzes the pairing susceptibility ($\chi$) through field-dependent band structure calculations (anticrossings), and concludes by matching the resulting phase diagram to UTe2's experimental observations.
why_interesting: The mechanism relies heavily on how SOC modifies electronic bands under external fields, leading to enhanced pairing channels—a concept relevant to understanding exotic superconductivity in strongly correlated materials where orbital degrees of freedom are crucial.
